questions.question: The SI unit of a physical quantity is pascal-second. Write pascal-second in SI base units, and hence write the dimensional formula of the quantity. Options from the paper: (A) [M L^{-1} T^{-1}] (B) [M L T^{-2}] (C) [M T^{-1}] (D) [M^{-1} L^3 T]. Find the correct dimensional formula.

Sometimes it is convenient to construct a system of units so that all quantities can be expressed in terms of only one physical quantity X. In one such system, [position] = [X^α], [speed] = [X^β], [acceleration] = [X^p], [linear momentum] = [X^q], [force] = [X^r]. Which of the following is/are correct? (A) α + p = 2β (B) p + q − r = β (C) p − q + r = α (D) p + q + r = β.

In a new system of units, the units of mass, length, time and current are 5 kg, 5 m, 5 s and 5 A, respectively. If μ0 and ε0 are the permeability and permittivity of free space, find the magnitude of one SI unit of √(μ0/ε0) in this new system.
Express 1 newton in SI base units. Then convert 1 N into dyne using 1 kg = 10^3 g and 1 m = 10^2 cm. This topic is derived units and conversion, not least count.
questions.notes: no bank item; authored. No self-contained derived-unit / SI-prefix conversion item survived OCR with usable numbers.

questions.notes: no bank item; authored. JEE Main/Advanced physics text has no AU / light-year / parsec item; eV hits are atomic/nuclear, not this practical-units slice.

Also, given 1 parsec = 3.26 ly, find how many astronomical units are in 1 parsec if 1 ly = 6.32 × 10^4 AU. Round the AU result to two significant figures.

questions.question: 10 divisions on the main scale of a vernier calliper coincide with 11 divisions on the vernier scale. If each main-scale division is 5 units, find the least count of the instrument. Options in the paper included 5/11 and 50/11; compute LC = 1 MSD − 1 VSD.

There are two vernier calipers, both with 1 cm divided into 10 equal main-scale divisions. On caliper C1, 10 vernier divisions correspond to 9 main-scale divisions. On caliper C2, 10 vernier divisions correspond to 11 main-scale divisions. Find the least count of each caliper (including the retrograde vernier C2).

The smallest division on the main scale of a vernier calipers is 0.1 cm. Ten divisions of the vernier scale correspond to nine divisions of the main scale. Find the least count. The zero-error configuration and a sphere held between the jaws are shown in the original paper; using that figure the correct diameter of the sphere is one of (A) 3.07 cm (B) 3.11 cm (C) 3.15 cm (D) 3.17 cm. State the least count first, then identify the diameter if the figure is available, otherwise stop after the least count.
A rod is known to be 2.00 m long. Four students report 1.8 m, 1.8 m, 1.9 m, and 1.8 m. Are these measurements precise, accurate, both, or neither? Define accuracy and precision in your explanation.
questions.notes: no bank item; authored. Bank has one ‘accuracy in g’ numerical (used as hard); no qualitative accuracy-vs-precision item.

questions.question: An event lasts exactly 10.00 s. Stopwatch A records 10.2 s, 10.1 s, 10.2 s, 10.1 s. Stopwatch B records 9.4 s, 10.8 s, 10.1 s, 9.7 s. Compare the two instruments in accuracy and in precision.
questions.notes: no bank item; authored. Same gap as easy; bank ‘accuracy’ hit is the pendulum-g percentage below.

questions.question: The measured length of a simple pendulum is 20 cm with 2 mm accuracy. The time for 50 oscillations was measured to be 40 seconds with 1 second resolution. From these measurements, the accuracy in g is N%. Find N. Options: 6, 4, 8, 5.

Classify each of the following as a systematic error or a random error, and give a one-line reason: (i) a metre scale whose zero end is worn down, (ii) scatter in repeated timings of a pendulum with a handheld stopwatch.
questions.notes: no bank item; authored. Bank has no ‘systematic/random/gross error’ classification item.

questions.question: A student always starts the stopwatch about 0.2 s late. Name the type of error and explain whether averaging many identical trials will remove it. Then contrast that with random scatter from reaction time that sometimes starts early and sometimes late.
questions.notes: no bank item; authored. Bank has no ‘systematic/random/gross error’ classification item.

questions.question: In a metre-bridge experiment the resistance wire is not uniform along its length. Identify the error as systematic, random, or a mix, explain why it is not a simple zero error, and describe one experimental change that reduces it.
questions.notes: no bank item; authored. Bank has no ‘systematic/random/gross error’ classification item.

questions.question: A student uses a simple pendulum of exactly 1 m length to determine g. He uses a stop watch with least count 1 s and records 40 seconds for 20 oscillations. Which of the following is/are true? (A) Error ΔT in measuring the time period T is 0.05 s (B) Error ΔT in measuring T is 1 s (C) Percentage error in g is 5% (D) Percentage error in g is 2.5%. Compute ΔT, ΔT/T, and Δg/g = 2 ΔT/T (L is exact).

A silver wire has mass (0.6 ± 0.006) g, radius (0.5 ± 0.005) mm and length (4 ± 0.04) cm. Find the maximum percentage error in its density. Options: (A) 4% (B) 3% (C) 6% (D) 7%. Use ρ = m / (π r² L) so Δρ/ρ = Δm/m + 2 Δr/r + ΔL/L.

The dimensions of a cone are measured using a scale with least count 2 mm. The diameter of the base and the height are both measured to be 20.0 cm. Find the maximum percentage error in the volume of the cone.
For z = a x^7 y^2, where a is a constant, the percentage errors in x and y are 4% and 12% respectively. Find the percentage error in z.

The energy of a system as a function of time t is E(t) = A² exp(−α t), where α = 0.2 s^{-1}. The measurement of A has an error of 1.25%. If the error in the measurement of time is 1.50%, find the percentage error in E at t = 5 s.

In an experiment to determine g, the period is T = 2π √((R − r)/g) with R = (60 ± 1) mm and r = (10 ± 1) mm. Five successive measurements of T are 0.52 s, 0.56 s, 0.57 s, 0.54 s and 0.59 s. The least count of the watch is 0.01 s. Which of the following is/are true? (A) The error in r is 10% (B) The error in T is 3.57% (C) The error in T is 2% (D) The error in the determined g is 11%. Combine the errors in R, r and T.
A student performs a titration with different burettes and finds titre values of 25.2 mL, 25.25 mL, and 25.0 mL. Find the number of significant figures in the average titre value.

A person measures masses of three particles as 435.42 g, 226.3 g and 0.125 g. According to the rules for arithmetic operations with significant figures, the addition of the three masses will be: (A) 661.845 g (B) 662 g (C) 661.84 g (D) 661.8 g. Choose the correct value.

Length, breadth and thickness of a strip of uniform cross section are measured to be 10.5 cm, 0.05 mm and 6.0 μm respectively. Which option(s) give the volume in cm³ with correct significant figures? (A) 3.2 × 10^{-5} (B) 32.0 × 10^{-6} (C) 3.0 × 10^{-5} (D) 3 × 10^{-5}.
Write the dimensional formulae of force, pressure, and kinetic energy in M, L, T. Then show that pressure and energy density have the same dimensions.
questions.notes: no bank item; authored. Pascal-second bank stem is used under units-systems; this slice is [F], [p], [K].

questions.question: Find the dimensional formula of angular impulse. Options in the paper were of the form [M L² T^{-1}] and [M L T^{-1}]. Start from angular impulse = change in angular momentum = [M L² T^{-1}].

Identify the pair of physical quantities that have the same dimensions: (A) velocity gradient and decay constant (B) Wien’s constant and Stefan’s constant (C) angular frequency and angular momentum (D) wave number and Avogadro number.

Statement I: Planck’s constant and angular momentum have the same dimensions. Statement II: Linear momentum and moment of force have the same dimensions. Which is true? Options: both true; both false; I true II false; I false II true.

Using the same four pairs as the dimensions-hard item is not allowed. Instead: check whether v = u + at and s = ut + at² are dimensionally homogeneous. Restore the missing 1/2 in the second equation by requiring every term to have dimension of length.
questions.notes: no bank item; authored. Second homogeneity numerical would duplicate the Planck/pair items; this is the textbook check those MCQs assume.

questions.question: A length-scale ℓ depends on the permittivity ε of a dielectric, Boltzmann constant k_B, temperature T, number density n of charged particles, and charge q on each. Which expression(s) for ℓ is/are dimensionally correct? (A) ℓ = [n q² / (ε k_B T)]^{1/2} (B) ℓ = [ε k_B T / (n q²)]^{1/2} (C) ℓ = [q² / (ε k_B T)]^{1/2} (D) ℓ = [q² / (ε n^{2/3} k_B T)]^{1/2}.
Assume the period T of a simple pendulum depends only on length ℓ and g as T = k ℓ^a g^b with k dimensionless. Use dimensional analysis to find a and b.
questions.notes: no bank item; authored. Bank dimensional-analysis items are the fog-signal and plasma-frequency problems (medium/hard).

questions.question: To find the distance d over which a signal can be seen clearly in foggy conditions, a railway engineer uses dimensional analysis and assumes that d depends on the mass density ρ of the fog, the intensity S (power/area) of the light, and its frequency f. The engineer finds that d is proportional to S^{1/n}. Find n.

A dense collection of equal numbers of electrons and positive ions is a neutral plasma. Let N be the number density of free electrons, each of mass m. When displaced and released they oscillate at the plasma frequency ω_p. Taking electronic charge e and permittivity ε0, use dimensional analysis to choose the correct expression for ω_p among forms built from N, e, m, ε0 (the paper’s options are equivalent to ω_p = sqrt(N e² / (ε0 m)) and three dimensionally wrong variants).
The displacement formula s = ut + (1/2) at² contains a factor 1/2. Explain why dimensional analysis cannot produce that 1/2, even though it can check that both terms are lengths.
